scripts.capture.js: Capture any Scholar page as PDF/HTML/PNG.
scripts.list-all-publications.js: Expand and export the full publication list with citation counts and URLs.
scripts.capture-citations.js: Capture every page of a citing-articles list, classify independence, highlight, and emit one PDF per page plus a review sheet.
scripts.run-batch.js: Sequential batch driver over the publication list: selection by citation range or title, --skip-done resume, --dry-run preview, and a progress record per publication.
scripts.summarize-progress.js: Rolls the per-page report JSON up into per-publication totals, counting only publications whose exhibit PDF is still filed. Run before reporting any count.
scripts.test-pdf-fit.js: Offline check that a citing page still fits one US Letter sheet at the exhibit print scale, using a saved HTML copy.
scripts.human.js: Shared pacing: randomized waits, stepped mouse moves, uneven scrolling.
scripts.name-match.js: Author matching on surname plus initials.
scripts.crosscheck.js: External corroboration of author lists: PubMed (NCBI E-utilities) first, then OpenAlex. No account required.
scripts.test-name-match.js: Offline tests for the matching rules (22 cases).
scripts.test-capture-helpers.js: Offline tests for count parsing, language detection, pagination offsets, end-of-list decisions, highlight and attention rules (62 cases). The language cases pin the 2026-11-01 rule: a CJK title containing a Greek notation letter is still non-English, a Polish title in Latin Extended-A is caught, a German abstract under an English title is NOT flagged, and Greek notation in a snippet does not suppress a citation.
scripts.test-next-link.js: Offline diagnosis of a truncated citing list: runs the capture's own pagination extraction and end-of-list verdict against a saved HTML copy. Contacts nothing.
scripts.tally.js: Shared counting rules (what counts as independent, per-publication grouping, exhibit-page estimate). Used by both summarize-progress.js and build-ledger.js so the two can never report different numbers for the same evidence. Also holds the language-edition rule: markLanguageEditions keys a work on the article id inside its DOI plus an author signature, so a publisher's translation (10.1002/anie.7795967 vs 10.1002/ange.7795967) is recognised even when its title is translated, and isHighlighted refuses any row marked duplicate_of. Requiring both a DOI and an identical author list keeps it conservative; a pair sharing the identical DOI is the ordinary duplicate-version case and is deliberately not claimed as an edition. Since 2026-11-01 groupReports resolves the editions itself, walking each publication's pages in order with one carried map, so every reader of groupReports (ledger, catalog, audit) agrees without each re-implementing the walk - that centralisation removed a 44-vs-46 disagreement between the ledger and the catalog. isWithheldForLanguage(e) is the mirror of isHighlighted for the rows a translation would recover, and tallyEntries reports the English-only figures (english_records, english_independent, unique_english_records, unique_english_independent) alongside the headline ones.
scripts.build-ledger.js: Builds the statistics log: one row per publication (independent, dependent, self-citation, review, coverage, non-English withheld, English-only records and independents) plus global totals, written as a dated JSON and a CSV that opens in a spreadsheet. Publications not yet captured are listed as not-started so the denominator is visible. Appends one line per run to citation-ledger-history.csv. Run after every batch, and after any reapply-language or reprint-exhibits run. Since 2026-11-01 it also prints the adjusted English-only total and percentage the guide asks for when no translations are obtained.
scripts.check-browser.js: Offline check of which browser the pipeline actually launches: runs the capture's own launcher, prints the version, executable path and user agent, and warns on a silent fallback away from the Chrome channel. Makes no network request.
scripts.unblock.js: Opens a page in the pipeline's own browser profile and waits, with no deadline, for the user to clear a verification screen. Exists because a batch run polls a wall for three minutes then closes the window, which is right unattended but leaves nothing to solve when someone returns. --check-only reports access and closes. Never attempts to solve or auto-retry a challenge.
scripts.work-type.js: Separates citing patents from citing articles. Only positive evidence counts: a patent-server link (Google Patents, USPTO, Espacenet) or a venue string naming a patent document. Title and snippet are deliberately NOT scanned, so a journal article about patents is not misfiled as one; a venue that merely contains the word 'patents' (for example the journal Expert Opinion on Therapeutic Patents) is returned as work_type 'unknown' for a human to settle rather than guessed either way.
scripts.test-work-type.js: Offline tests for the patent/article classifier (28 checks). Includes the regression case for an article about patents, the four captured patent records, and a guard that the scanned fields stay limited to the venue carriers.
scripts.build-catalog.js: Builds Database/citation-catalog.sqlite (a folder at the project root, deliberately outside Exhibits, which is the evidence folder that gets reviewed and filed), a read-only lookup layer over every report JSON plus the publication snapshot. Full rebuild is idempotent; --pub=<base> upserts one publication and is called by run-batch.js after each capture. Keeps every observed row, including superseded captures, with a filed flag so a query can widen; stores the derived work_type, patent number, is_highlighted and is_primary_copy columns. Ends by recounting through tally.js and comparing to the database, so any drift from the ledger rule is reported rather than hidden. A blocked capture with no report file writes nothing.
scripts.query-catalog.js: Read-only query CLI over the citation catalog: patents | editions | nonenglish | stats | search | pub | review | sql | tables. --csv for spreadsheet output, --all to include unfiled and archived captures, --limit=N to widen. Opens the database read-only and the sql subcommand accepts SELECT only, refusing writes, schema changes and stacked statements. Default totals are filed-only so they match the ledger. 'editions' lists each citing list where one article appears in two languages, naming the copy the exhibit marks and the copy held back; it changes no counted figure. 'nonenglish' lists the entries the language screen holds back with the reason and whether the row would otherwise have counted - the list a certified translation would have to cover. stats prints the adjusted English-only totals next to the headline ones.
scripts.audit-highlights.js: Offline check that every filed exhibit page still carries exactly the marks the current rules call for. Replays the rule over each saved page's HTML in a headless browser with every network request aborted, comparing the yellow marks actually present row by row against tally.isHighlighted, and confirming the exhibit PDF exists and is non-empty. Exists because the PDF is a picture while the ledger reads the report JSON: when the counting rule changes, only this comparison notices a filed exhibit now disagrees. Read-only, exits 1 on any mismatch.
scripts.reapply-language.js: Offline rule application for the language screen. Recomputes language_flag over the filed report JSON using the current capture-citations.js rule, preserving the value captured at capture time in a new language_flag_captured field so the original is never lost. Dry-run by default; --write backs every file it touches up to Exhibits/Supporting/Pre-rule-reapply-<date>/ before saving, prints each mark flip as ADD or DROP, and lists the exhibit pages that then need re-printing. Exists because a rule fix in the capture script cannot reach exhibits already captured - their flags were written at capture time. --all widens to archived and unfiled reports. No Scholar request is made.
scripts.reprint-exhibits.js: Offline re-print of an exhibit page from its saved HTML, for when the counting rule changes but the capture must not be repeated. Loads the saved page in a headless browser with every network request aborted, strips all title backgrounds, re-applies tally.isHighlighted using the same row matching capture-citations.js uses, and refuses to save unless the marks it applied equal the count the rule expects. Rewrites the HTML (backing the original up first), archives the old PDF to Exhibits/Archive/SUPERSEDED-<base>.pdf, writes the new PDF at the exhibit print settings (US Letter, 75% scale, header from report.cites_url plus the snapshot date, footer with page numbers) and a fresh PNG. --page= / --pub= select one page, --changed re-prints every page whose marks drifted, --check reports without writing.

capture_tooling.pagination: Scholar shows 10 citing articles per page for this profile and a pagesize=20 parameter does not change it, so the capture follows each page's own 'Next' link, which carries Scholar's real step size and its as_sdt/sciodt/scipsc parameters. Hand-built start= offsets drop those parameters and skip records. Each page is saved as its own PDF; page 1 keeps the plain name and later pages take a -p2, -p3 suffix. 24 of the 48 publications have more than 20 citations, so this is required rather than optional. The header count is a cross-check only, because Scholar counts duplicate versions that per-record dedupe removes.
capture_tooling.auto_mode: --auto saves each page without waiting for ENTER. The browser stays visible so a verification screen is still seen. On an access wall in --auto mode the script re-reads the already-open page only, making no new requests, and stops after three minutes with exit code 2 rather than hanging on a prompt nobody is there to answer.
capture_tooling.batch_run_log: Exhibits/Supporting/batch-runs.json records every publication attempted: cites id, pages captured versus expected, records and independent count, exit code, and whether it was blocked. An interrupted batch resumes with --skip-done. Since 2026-10-31 the batch driver also refreshes the citation catalog for each publication after writing the run log, and skips that step for a blocked attempt, which wrote no report and so cannot change the database.
capture_tooling.citation_catalog: Database/citation-catalog.sqlite at the project root is the PRIMARY durable store for the citation rows, built and maintained by tools/build-catalog.js and queried with tools/query-catalog.js. Its full schema is documented in Database/citation-catalog-schema.md. Kept out of Exhibits on purpose: that folder is the evidence packet. DO NOT DELETE IT - it holds row history the report JSON does not, and tools/build-catalog.js merges into it rather than replacing it. Every row carries a permanent row_uid (cit-000106 style) that is minted once and never reused, so a uid quoted today means the same row after a re-capture or a rebuild; the integer id column is a frozen legacy alias and is not quoted. A row whose exhibit is archived or re-captured is retired with superseded_at and a reason, never deleted. Retained verified snapshots are written to Database/Backups before any write, and that folder is tracked in git. Rebuilt offline on 2026-11-02 at schema version 4 and reconciling against the derived report on all fifteen checks: 41 of 48 publications, 168 filed exhibit pages, 1498 active records over 1480 distinct papers, 1030 countable independent (1017 distinct, 653 externally confirmed), 322 dependent, 0 self (PI), 5 self (former PI), 94 awaiting review, 52 flagged non-English of which 44 are withheld from the count by language alone. v_review holds the 94 unresolved rows in three buckets - 6 contradicted, 13 external-shows-no-overlap, 75 unresolvable - and is what tools/query-catalog.js review, tools/build-review-sheet.js and the dashboard's review section all read, so they name the same rows. It also answers questions the report JSON does not: 15 citing patents and applications across 7 publications, 8 counted as independent, kept separate from the article citations.

capture_tooling.statistics_log: tools/tally.js holds the single definition of what counts and every report uses it: summarize-progress.js, build-ledger.js, run-batch.js and capture-citations.js. Two row counts are reported on purpose - rows on the exhibit pages, and distinct papers after Scholar's duplicate versions collapse. Quote the distinct-paper figure when stating how many papers cite the work. A --no-crosscheck run is a working copy: its independent citations are not counted. Since 2026-11-02 the direction is settled the other way round from earlier notes: Database/citation-catalog.sqlite is the primary store of the rows, and citation-ledger-<snapshot>.csv written by tools/build-ledger.js is a DERIVED REPORT of those rows. build-ledger.js reads the active rows out of the store, recomputes the same figures independently from the report JSON, and compares them figure by figure; a disagreement is a defect to investigate, is resolved in neither side's favour, exits 4, and writes nothing. So the CSV is still what a packet figure is quoted from - it is the dated, reviewable report - but it can no longer be right while the store is wrong, because the two are checked against each other on every run and no figure may be quoted from a run that failed. A language edition of a paper already on the same citing list is recorded and never marked or counted, per the user's instruction on 2026-10-31 that such duplicates be documented in the database and not highlighted in the exhibits. The adjusted English-only figures added on 2026-11-01 divide English independent citations by the English citation records observed on the filed citing lists; Scholar publishes no English-only profile total, and the ledger's note field states that rather than leaving it implied.

independence_rules.definition: A citing paper is independent only when it shares no author with the cited paper.
independence_rules.self_citation_pi: Richard D. Cummings (current PI) - never counted as independent, even on papers the user did not co-author.
independence_rules.self_citation_former_pi: Umesh R. Desai (former PI) - never counted as independent, even on papers the user did not co-author.
independence_rules.name_matching: Surname plus initials, never surname alone, because Desai and Cummings are common. A surname collision without comparable initials is flagged for manual review rather than counted or excluded.
independence_rules.non_english: Per the guide, a non-English citation must not be highlighted and cannot count toward the adjusted total without a certified human translation and affidavit; machine translation is explicitly not certified. The guide defines 'listed in English' as the title of the article, the list of authors and the venue - not the body - which is why the screen keys on the TITLE (user's option B, applied 2026-11-01), while a non-Latin script anywhere in the entry, snippet included, still flags it. Greek letters are treated as scientific notation, not evidence of a foreign paper: an alpha-1,2-mannosidase title is English. So NON_LATIN excludes the Greek range, ACCENTED spans Latin Extended-A/B as well as Latin-1, and FOREIGN_WORDS is scanned on the title only. The flag is a conservative screen, not a ruling, and flagged entries are listed in the review sheet for a human decision. Per the user's decision on 2026-11-01 no translations are obtained: flagged entries stay unhighlighted and out of the totals, and the packet reports an adjusted independent total and percentage based solely on English citations, as the guide's second path allows.
independence_rules.author_list_source: Google Scholar only: the cited paper's profile article page for its authors, and for citing entries the result snippet plus, where Scholar truncated it, the BibTeX record behind that result's Cite control. Third-party databases are not used as the basis for independence.
independence_rules.external_corroboration: Per user instruction on 2026-10-29, every entry Scholar leaves looking independent is additionally checked against PubMed (NCBI E-utilities esearch/esummary) and, failing that, OpenAlex, both of which publish the complete author list. Google Scholar remains the primary source, so the external look-up corroborates rather than decides. confirm_state values: confirmed (external list agrees there is no overlap); unverified-coverage (not indexed externally, Scholar's own list complete, still highlighted and flagged for a spot-check - typical of theses, preprints and patents); unresolved (not indexed and Scholar's list truncated, so not highlighted); contradicted (external list shows a shared or PI author, entry pulled back to REVIEW and never marked). An entry is never promoted to independent on an external record alone. CrossRef is deliberately excluded as a basis for any independence call.
independence_rules.corroboration_credentials: Neither PubMed nor OpenAlex needs an account or token, and both were verified working anonymously on 2026-10-29. NCBI's usage policy asks for an identifying email and offers an optional API key that raises the limit from 3 to 10 requests/second. Both are optional for this tool because requests are few, sequential and paced. Supply with --email / --ncbi-key or the CROSSCHECK_EMAIL / NCBI_API_KEY environment variables; the email is also sent to OpenAlex as mailto for the polite pool.
independence_rules.highlight_key: In the exhibit PDF: yellow = confirmed independent, and nothing else is marked. Entries awaiting review are unmarked and listed in the review Markdown. The orange/faded marks and the on-page legend appear only in --debug working copies.
